evals.name: development-storage-to-production
evals.prompt: Our Compose file runs latest-development. We changed to latest, set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development, and reused MongoDB. What must be checked before exposing it? Explain without deploying or printing secrets.
evals.expected_output: DEVELOPMENT is compile-time, production requires explicit storage and TLS/encryption certificates subject to authority exceptions, reused storage retains development OAuth application.
assertions: Explains DEVELOPMENT is a Debug compile-time symbol and cannot be enabled through ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT.

Names production storage, TLS and internal-authority encryption certificate prerequisites and the external/disabled authority exception without claiming value encryption no longer needs a certificate.
Warns the known development application persists in reused storage and must be removed from storage and any recreating configuration before exposure.

evals.name: private-h2c-and-probe
evals.prompt: We terminate HTTPS at an ingress. Can Tls.Enabled=false, ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true and a plaintext health port make Chronicle ready? Explain protocol, auth, trust and health exposure at 19.50.0.
evals.expected_output: Private h2c only, all upstream traffic HTTP/2, external HTTPS authority and no SDK external ClientCredentials support, restricted immediate proxy trust, health exclusive defaults false.
assertions: Requires private HTTP/2-only h2c upstream for all traffic and restricted direct backend access, not public plaintext or HTTP/1.1 upstream.
States forwarded headers trust loopback or configured immediate proxies/networks only; the ASPNETCORE switch does not widen trust and the proxy must replace client headers.
Explains internal OAuth/token endpoint is unavailable in authenticated h2c and the .NET SDK ClientCredentials external-authority limitation.
Warns a dedicated plaintext health port exposes other HTTP/1.1 endpoints by default and recommends internal access plus health.exclusive=true.

evals.name: shared-storage-is-not-membership
evals.prompt: Two production containers share a MongoDB replica set and leave clustering at its default. We also deploy a changed reducer under PartialOnly. Are we one cluster and will history be rebuilt automatically? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Localhost creates separate clusters; MongoDB membership on every node with same ids, reducer fingerprints classify replay, PartialOnly recommends full replay instead of performing it.
assertions: Explains shared MongoDB does not turn default Localhost membership into one cluster and requires clustering.type=MongoDB on every node with shared cluster/service ids.
States only MongoDB supports multi-node storage and MongoDB must be a replica set.
Explains reducer code fingerprint changes can require full replay and PartialOnly leaves a recommendation rather than automatically rebuilding full history.
